# About ICA Political Communication Summer School

### The Lectures

The School brings together world-leading researchers in Political Communication to address key theoretical and empirical questions at the intersection of political communication, political science, and political sociology. Through lectures, workshops, and intensive feedback sessions, participants engage with cutting-edge research on the relationships between political communication, media, political participation, and democracy, while developing their own projects under the close mentorship of leading scholars in the field.

:::

::: {.content-block}

### The Faculty

The 2026 Faculty gathers internationally renowned academics to engage with students. Confirmed in-person speakers include: Dr. Christian Baden (The Hebrew University of Jerusalem), Dr. Dam Hee Kim (Korea University), Dr. Regina Lawrence (University of Oregon), Dr. Joerg Matthes (University of Vienna), Dr. Patricia Moy (University of Washington), Dr. Chris Fei Shen (City University of Hong Kong), Dr. Lone Sorensen (University of Leeds), Dr. Talia Stroud (University of Texas at Austin), Dr. Sebastián Valenzuela (Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile), Dr. Claes de Vreese (University of Amsterdam).


:::

::: {.content-block}

### The Students

Participants come from around the globe; countries represented at previous Summer Schools include USA, Canada, Colombia, Brazil, UK, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Latvia, Russia, Poland, Germany, The Netherlands, France, Spain, Portugal, Italy, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Serbia, Turkey, Pakistan, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa among others.

### A Successful Experience

Building on the experience of the last 15 years, the 2026 Summer School offers a unique opportunity for 30 PhD candidates and early career academics in communication, political science, sociology, and psychology:

1. to attend an intensive, five-day program that consists of lectures, master classes, paper presentations, and mentoring sessions, and  
2. to build long-lasting personal and scholarly relations in a celebrated, friendly, and productive environment.

:::
